What It Is
WUT it IZ
interjection (Boomer slang)
A 1970s African-American greeting, "What it is!" (often answered "What it was!" or "What it is, brother!"), roughly "Hello, what’s happening?", carried into general slang by television and film of the decade. The fuller "It is what it is" (resigned acceptance) is a separate, later expression that became common in the 2000s.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

What it is! was a 1970s greeting — a cool way to say hello and "what’s going on?" at once. Two friends meet on the street: "What it is!" "What it is, man." The Christian observation: a greeting is a small thing that Scripture takes seriously, because a greeting can carry a blessing. When Boaz walked into his barley field, he greeted his workers, "The LORD be with you," and they answered him, "The LORD bless thee" (Rut 2:4). That is a greeting with God in it. The priests of Israel greeted the people with the great benediction: "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace" (Num 6:24–26). The Psalmist mourns the passersby who never say, "The blessing of the LORD be upon you" (Psa 129:8). John opens a letter, "Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth" (3Jn 1:2). The modern greeting has shrunk to "hey" and "what’s up," and the old 1970s "what it is" was at least warm. A Christian can be warmer still. "A word spoken in due season, how good is it!" (Pro 15:23). A father who greets his children in the morning with a blessing is doing what Boaz did in the field.

Webster 1828 Definition

1970s AAVE greeting ("What it is!"), roughly "Hello, what’s happening?" — a warm hello Scripture can fill with blessing, as Boaz greeted his reapers: "The LORD be with you" (Rut 2:4).

expand to see more

WHAT IT IS, interj. (AAVE, 1970s; Boomer era) A greeting: hello; what’s happening? Reply often "What it is!" or "What it was!"

Distinct from it is what it is (2000s), an expression of resigned acceptance.

Decode for families: greetings matter. Teach your children one with a blessing in it.

Key Scripture

Rut 2:4 — "And, behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said unto the reapers, The LORD be with you. And they answered him, The LORD bless thee."

Num 6:24 — "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee:"

Num 6:25 — "The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee:"

Num 6:26 — "The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace."

Psa 129:8 — "Neither do they which go by say, The blessing of the LORD be upon you: we bless you in the name of the LORD."

3Jn 1:2 — "Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth."

Modern Corruption

A harmless and friendly greeting; Scripture shows how much more a greeting can carry when it brings the blessing of the LORD.

expand to see more

There is nothing to correct in what it is; it is a friendly hello. The modern cousin, it is what it is, deserves a gentler critique: it is a shrug of fatalism, the language of a world without providence. The Christian never quite says "it is what it is," because he knows Who governs what is and that all things work together for good to them that love God.

The positive lesson is Ruth 2:4. In a farm field in Bethlehem, a landowner and his workers greeted each other in the name of the LORD, and the whole book of Ruth unfolds from that field of mutual blessing. A family that greets one another, and its neighbors, with a word of blessing is practicing a lost art that the Bible treats as worship.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

1970s AAVE greeting What it is! (reply What it was!); distinct from 2000s it is what it is.

expand to see more

1970s African-American vernacular: What it is! — a greeting

Common replies: What it is!, What it was!

1970s television and film carry it into general slang

2000s: it is what it is — a separate, fatalistic expression

Hebrew barak — to bless; the greeting of Rut 2:4

Usage

""Grandpa walked into the barbershop and said, ‘What it is!’ The barber said, ‘What it was!’ They’ve been friends since 1974.""

"The LORD be with you. And they answered him, The LORD bless thee (Rut 2:4)."

"The LORD bless thee, and keep thee (Num 6:24)."
